subject: design
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Concept of the skill, Coverage, Philosophy of the skill, Verification, Do NOT Use When) and the canonical design-thinking literature (d.school five stages, UK Design Council Double Diamond, IDEO arc, Knapp Design Sprint).

cases.scenario: A team has a fat folder of user-interview transcripts and a deadline. They want to start sketching screens this week because 'we've talked to enough users.'
cases.context: No problem statement, no synthesis artifact, and no agreed definition of what they are solving exists yet.
cases.question: How should the agent guide the next move?
expected_flags: Recognizes they are post-discover but pre-define — raw data, no framed problem
Flags jumping to sketching (ideate/prototype) as stage skipping
Routes to research-synthesis (affinity mapping) then problem-framing before ideation
Names the open question: what problem is actually worth solving?
expected_fix_hints: Run a synthesis pass to turn transcripts into themes and insights
Write a framed problem statement before any screen sketching
absent_signals: Do not start sketching screens before synthesis and framing
Do not treat 'we talked to enough users' as a transition criterion

cases.scenario: After a usability test, three of five participants revealed the team had framed the wrong job-to-be-done. The PM wants to ship the prototype anyway 'because we're out of runway.'
cases.context: The prototype tests well on the wrong problem; the findings contradict the Define-stage framing.
cases.question: How should the agent respond?
expected_flags: Applies the loop-back principle — a Test finding invalidated the Define stage
Recommends an explicit decision to loop back to define rather than ship as-is
Records the loop-back rationale rather than silently dropping the contradicting finding
Names shipping despite contradicting evidence as performing the ritual, not practicing it
expected_fix_hints: Re-frame the problem against the new evidence, then re-ideate narrowly
Scope a minimal re-test rather than a full new arc if runway is tight
absent_signals: Do not ship the prototype against the contradicting findings without a recorded decision
Do not treat 'out of runway' as a reason to skip the loop-back judgment

cases.scenario: A team has run four rounds of interviews and three reframing workshops over two months and has built nothing. Each round 'raises new questions.'
cases.context: Leadership is frustrated; the team equates research activity with progress.
cases.question: How should the agent intervene?
expected_flags: Identifies stage stalling — researching and reframing indefinitely
Names that the team is mistaking activity for progress
Recommends naming 'we have enough' and advancing to ideation/prototyping
Sets a written transition criterion so the next stage has a done condition
expected_fix_hints: Write the current framed problem and commit to it for one prototype cycle
Define what evidence would make further research worthwhile before running it
absent_signals: Do not authorize another open-ended research round without a transition criterion
Do not treat new questions alone as a reason to keep looping

cases.scenario: A vague brief arrives: 'help us figure out what to build for new homeowners.' A junior asks which design-thinking method to run first.
cases.context: The team is at the very start with no user evidence and no framed problem.
cases.question: How should the agent route the work?
expected_flags: Locates them at the start of the arc (discover/empathize)
Routes first to user-research, not ideation or prototyping
Names the open question and the artifact each stage should produce before advancing
Plans the arc forward (research -> synthesis -> framing -> ideation) rather than picking a method at random
expected_fix_hints: Start with user-research to gather real homeowner evidence
Sequence synthesis and problem-framing before any concept generation
absent_signals: Do not jump straight to brainstorming solutions on a vague brief
Do not pick a method without naming the open question it answers

cases.scenario: A startup has one week before an investor demo and an untested core concept. They ask whether to run a full multi-month design process.
cases.context: Time is the binding constraint; the concept's core assumption is unvalidated.
cases.question: What format should the agent recommend?
expected_flags: Recommends a compressed Design Sprint over a multi-month arc given the time constraint
Names the trade-off: the sprint buys speed of learning at the cost of research depth
Targets a Define-through-Test cycle in days to validate the core assumption
Notes both formats are valid; the choice follows from uncertainty and time pressure
expected_fix_hints: Run a 5-day sprint focused on the single riskiest assumption
Defer breadth research to after the demo if the core concept survives
absent_signals: Do not start a multi-month arc when a one-week sprint fits the constraint

cases.scenario: An engineering lead asks the design-thinking owner to model the bounded contexts and event flows for the order-fulfillment domain, calling it 'discovery.'
cases.context: The word 'discovery' is overloaded; this is engineering domain modeling, not user discovery.
cases.question: How should the agent scope the request?
expected_flags: Recognizes this is engineering domain discovery, not human-centered discovery
Routes to event-storming / bounded-context-mapping / conceptual-modeling, not the design-thinking arc
Notes the empathy stage assumes human subjects; methods do not transfer to a system domain
Redirects rather than running the full arc out of lane
expected_fix_hints: Hand the domain modeling to event-storming and bounded-context-mapping
Reserve design thinking for the human-experience side if one exists
absent_signals: Do not run user-empathy methods on an internal system domain
Do not treat 'discovery' as automatically meaning the design-thinking arc
